thread:
Aisha: Heads up — noticed a perf regression on PP 1F1B after yesterday's kernel selector tweak. p99 latency jumps ~18% and overall throughput down ~12% on 4pp/2tp runs.

Daniel: Ugh. Is this across sequence lengths or only long sequences?

Aisha: Mostly long sequences (seq=1024+). Shorter seqs look fine. KV hit rate is the same. Appears when microbatch=2, microbatch=4 shows smaller delta.

Ravi: Any flamegraphs or heatmaps? Can you paste perf-bot traces? :eyes:

Aisha: perf-bot attached trace (summary):
- allreduce time increased 2.3x in backward pass
- idle bubble increases at stage 2->3 boundary
- kernel fallback to generic CUDA kernel for attention on tail tokens

perf-bot: [perf-trace] https://internal.perf/reports/1839998888/summary (flamegraph + timeline)

Marta: Looks like the kernel selection heuristic started choosing the "split-attn-fallback" path when avg_seq > 900 because we disabled the contiguity check. That creates non-contiguous tensors for allreduce -> causes NCCL to fall back to algorithm with more latency.

Kai: Can we force contiguous_allreduce on the fast path and test? I remember a patch that added a safe copy but it was gated behind an env flag.

Aisha: I reproduced locally with this cmd:
```
./load_test --model redwood-7b --pp=4 --tp=2 --microbatch=2 --seq=1024 --profile --traces=perf
```
Flame shows allreduce overlap ~= 12% before change, now ~40% of step time.

Daniel: Quick mitigations to try: set microbatch=4, enable contiguous_allreduce=true, revert kernel selector change (revert CL 7891), or try enabling delayed-allreduce (move allreduce to overlap with next microbatch compute).

Ravi: I ran microbatch=4 — throughput improved and p99 back near baseline. So bubble size interacts with the kernel path.

Marta: The root cause: selector used heuristics purely based on seq length and attention pattern, but didn't consider tensor memory layout after kv cache concat. For 1F1B microbatch=2 the layout ends up non-contiguous. Need to update selector to check .is_contiguous() before picking the vectorized kernel.

Kai: I'll open a small revert PR for the selector and add a short-term env flag ENABLE_CONTIGUOUS_ALLREDUCE=true to prod canary. Who wants the revert?

Aisha: Assign to Kai for the revert. I'll run canary with microbatch=2 on dedicated infra and report metrics.

perf-bot: Canary scheduled on canary-pool-2, job id 7643. Expected run time 45m.

Daniel: Also add a perf unit test: run pp=4 tp=2 seq=1024 microbatch=2 and assert p99 doesn't regress >5% vs baseline. Put it behind nightly so we catch future selector changes.

Marta: Agreed. I'll add the continuity check and tests. We'll likely follow with an improved heuristic that folds in tensor layout and kv-cache concat cost.

Aisha: Thanks team. Timeline: Kai does revert+flag within 1h, Marta adds continuity check + unit test today, I'll run canary and post perf dashboards. If canary looks good we'll roll to prod tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: @channel Deploy window scheduled: revert-cl-7891 -> canary -> prod. Notifying SRE oncall.

Kai: On it. Patch coming in 10m.

Ravi: Nice sleuthing — good catch on the contiguity interaction.

Aisha: Closing the loop once canary completes.
